newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks up on bargain hunting, auction hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks up on bargain hunting, auction hopes.

text.p: Mexican stocks extended early gains to stand sharply up at mid-session on selective bargain-hunting driven by expected forthcoming cuts in primary interest rates, analysts and traders said.
"I feel the upswing can still be considered a technical rebound; the market is speculative," said Esteban Rojas, associate research director at the Arka brokerage.
"On the other hand, forecast cuts in primary rates and a firm peso could also be helping," he added.
The leading IPC share index was up 38.39 points shortly after mid-session, or 1.02 percent, at 3,803.27.
Money market traders forecast falls of up to 100 basis points on bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at the central bank's primary auction of government securities later in the day.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were meanwhile 2.4 centavos stronger at 7.8830/7.8860 per dollar.
Dealers said strong gains by the Dow Jones on Monday, when Mexican markets were closed, also bolstered the bourse.
"We also have to keep a close eye on the Dow Jones, Mexico is obviously a long way behind and very selective," a desk trader said.
The Dow Jones was meanwhile up 20.47 points at 7,234.96.
"There is not much paper and that is why volume is thin," the trader added.
Trading volume was moderate at 46.1 million shares.

Dealers said retail stocks were the strongest after being hit hard by the market. Retail chain Controladora Comercial Mexicana up 50 centavos to pesos, headed the prominent gainers' list. (( --Karina Balderas, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
